rationale: Payment for ordinary hours of work is the base case for qualifying earnings
Casual loading on ordinary hours counts in full
Shift penalties, including public holiday penalties, are included
Paid annual leave taken during employment counts
Leave loading demonstrably tied to a lost opportunity to work overtime is the one excluded case
Every other annual leave loading counts, the overtime link is the only exception
Long service leave counts unless it is paid under a portable scheme
Long service leave paid by a portable scheme administrator rather than the employer is excluded
Family and domestic violence leave counts, easy to miss since it is not widely publicised
Paid personal and carers leave counts
Employer paid parental leave is excluded
Workers compensation for hours actually worked or required to attend counts
Workers compensation while not required to work, including any top up pay, is excluded
Cashing out annual leave while still employed counts
Cashing out a rostered day off while still employed counts
Unused leave paid out on a normal termination is excluded
Task and skill type allowances, including first aid, count as ordinary time earnings
An expense allowance expected to be fully spent by the employee is excluded
A flat allowance paid regardless of the expense actually incurred counts, unlike a true reimbursement
Overtime is excluded once ordinary hours are clearly identified in an award or agreement
An on call allowance for hours outside ordinary hours is excluded
Cashing out time off in lieu is treated as overtime and excluded, unlike cashing out an RDO
All commission payments count
Commission counts even when earned entirely outside ordinary hours, one of the actual Payday Super changes
A discretionary Christmas bonus for ordinary hours work counts
A bonus paid solely for work entirely outside ordinary hours is excluded, the opposite outcome to the same scenario paid as a commission
Remuneration paid to a working director counts
Payment in lieu of notice counts regardless of the reason for termination
Genuine redundancy payments are excluded termination payments
Counts if the RDO is cashed out while still employed, excluded if paid out unused on termination, the code name alone cannot distinguish these
